question: In which year was Asha Bhosle's name entered into the Guinness Book of World Records for most studio recordings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2011.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asha Bhosle entered the Guinness Book of World Records in 2011 for having recorded the highest number of solo, duet and chorus-backed songs by any singer — over 11,000 songs in about 20 Indian languages since 1947. (आशा भोसले — सर्वाधिक स्टूडियो रिकॉर्डिंग, 2011)

 

• She was recognised as the "Most Recorded Artist" in music history, a title associated with her recording career spanning more than seven decades.

 

• Asha Bhosle is the younger sister of legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar and has sung across genres ranging from classical to cabaret, ghazals and pop.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• She received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2000 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2008 for her contribution to Indian cinema and music.

 

• Her famous songs include "Dum Maro Dum", "Chura Liya Hai Tumne" and "Piya Tu Ab To Aaja".

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (2017), Option 2 (2020) and Option 3 (2014): These years are incorrect; the Guinness recognition for Asha Bhosle's record number of studio recordings is dated to 2011, not any of these years.

question: Which article of Indian constitution is related with the Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 371F.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 371F of the Indian Constitution contains special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim, inserted by the 36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975, when Sikkim became a full-fledged state of India. (अनुच्छेद 371एफ — सिक्किम)

 

• It protects Sikkim's pre-merger laws, provides for a minimum number of seats for Sikkim in the Lok Sabha, and safeguards the rights and privileges of different sections of Sikkim's population.

 

• Article 371F falls under Part XXI of the Constitution, which deals with Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions for various states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 371 deals with special provisions for the states of Maharashtra and Gujarat (separate development boards for Vidarbha, Marathwada, Saurashtra and Kutch).

 

• Article 371A contains special provisions for Nagaland, protecting Naga customary law and procedure; Article 371C contains special provisions for the Hill Areas of Manipur.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 371C (Option 1): Relates to Manipur's Hill Areas, not Sikkim.

 

• Article 371 (Option 2): Relates to Maharashtra and Gujarat, not Sikkim.

 

• Article 371A (Option 4): Relates to Nagaland, not Sikkim.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct with respect to the Sangam literature?

I. These texts were supposed to be composed and compiled in assemblies of poets.

II. The Sangam literature compiled in assemblies of poets were held in the city of Madurai.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements about the Sangam literature are correct. (संगम साहित्य — मदुरै की सभाओं में रचित)

 

• Statement I is correct: The Sangam texts (Tamil poetic works of the early historic period) were composed and compiled in assemblies (Sangams) of poets and scholars, held under royal patronage.

 

• Statement II is correct: These assemblies of poets are traditionally held to have taken place in the city of Madurai, under the patronage of the Pandya kings.

 

• The Sangam age is traditionally dated from around 300 BCE to 300 CE, and the literature produced covers poetry, grammar (e.g., Tolkappiyam) and moral works (e.g., Tirukkural).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sangam literature is classified into two broad groups: the Ettuthokai (Eight Anthologies) and the Pattupattu (Ten Idylls).

 

• Tradition speaks of three Sangams (Muchchangam), with the first two believed to be held at earlier Pandya capitals and the third and most productive one at Madurai.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, as both statements are factually accurate.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, as it wrongly excludes Statement II, which is also correct.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, as it wrongly excludes Statement I, which is also correct.

question: Which of the following have mountain range young fold mountains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alps mountain range.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Alps are an example of young fold mountains, formed by the collision of the African and Eurasian tectonic plates during the Alpine orogeny, which began around 65 million years ago. (आल्प्स पर्वत — नवीन वलित पर्वत)

 

• Young fold mountains are geologically recent, have high, sharp, jagged peaks, and are still tectonically active.

 

• Other examples of young fold mountains include the Himalayas, Rockies and Andes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Old fold mountains are highly eroded, with low and rounded peaks, formed hundreds of millions of years ago; examples include the Aravallis, Appalachians, Urals and Scandinavian mountains.

 

• The Aravalli Range in India is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world, believed to be over 500 million years old.

 

NOTE

 

• Appalachians mountain range (Option 1): An old, eroded fold mountain range in eastern North America.

 

• Aravali mountain range (Option 3): One of the oldest fold mountain ranges in the world, located in India.

 

• Ural mountain range (Option 4): An old fold mountain range forming the traditional boundary between Europe and Asia.

question: Identify a fomite from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glass.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A fomite is any inanimate (non-living) object or material that, when contaminated with an infectious agent, can transfer disease to a new host. (फोमाइट — निर्जीव वस्तु जो संक्रमण फैलाती है)

 

• Glass (such as a drinking glass, window, or door handle) is a classic example of a fomite, as it is a non-living surface that can carry and transmit pathogens like viruses and bacteria.

 

• Other everyday fomites include doorknobs, clothing, utensils, toys and currency notes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diseases commonly transmitted via fomites include the common cold, COVID-19, and gastrointestinal infections like norovirus.

 

• Regular disinfection of frequently touched surfaces is an important public health measure to break fomite-based disease transmission.

 

NOTE

 

• Drinking water (Option 1): Water is typically a vehicle for water-borne disease transmission, not classified as a fomite.

 

• Blood (Option 2): A bodily fluid, not an inanimate object, so it is not classified as a fomite.

 

• Saliva (Option 3): A bodily fluid, not an inanimate object, so it is not classified as a fomite.

question: Kullu Dussehra is a colourful festival majorly celebrated in which state/union territory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kullu Dussehra is celebrated in the Kullu valley of Himachal Pradesh, and is famous for the grand procession of local deities (devta-devis) converging at the Dhalpur maidan. (कुल्लू दशहरा — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• Unlike Dussehra elsewhere in India, which typically ends with Ravana Dahan on Vijayadashami, Kullu Dussehra begins on Vijayadashami and continues for about seven days, centred on the deity Raghunathji (Lord Rama).

 

• It was included in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kullu Dussehra was started in the 17th century by local ruler Raja Jagat Singh of Kullu.

 

• Other notable Himachal Pradesh festivals include the Minjar Fair of Chamba.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi (Option 1), Telangana (Option 2) and Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): These regions celebrate Dussehra/Dasara in their own traditional forms, but the distinctive Kullu Dussehra festival is specific to Himachal Pradesh, not to any of these.

question: Peat coal has ______ carbon and ______ moisture content?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Low, high.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Peat is the first and lowest stage in the formation of coal from decayed plant matter, and it has the lowest carbon content (around 50–60%) and the highest moisture content among all coal varieties. (पीट कोयला — निम्न कार्बन, उच्च नमी)

 

• The coal formation sequence, in order of increasing carbon content and decreasing moisture, is: Peat → Lignite → Bituminous → Anthracite.

 

• Because of its low carbon and high moisture content, peat has a low calorific value and is not efficient as a fuel; it is often dried before use.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anthracite is the highest-grade coal, with the highest carbon content (up to 95%) and the lowest moisture content, giving it the highest calorific value.

 

• India's major coal reserves are largely of the bituminous and lignite type.

 

NOTE

 

• High, Low (Option 1) and High, High (Option 3): Both wrongly state peat has high carbon content, whereas peat actually has the lowest carbon content of all coal types.

 

• Low, Low (Option 4): Wrongly states peat has low moisture content, whereas peat actually has the highest moisture content of all coal types.

question: After the ______, Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chauri Chaura incidence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 5 February 1922 in Chauri Chaura, Uttar Pradesh (then United Provinces), when a violent mob set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. (चौरी चौरा कांड — असहयोग आंदोलन वापसी)

 

• Distressed by this outbreak of violence, which went against the principle of non-violence (ahimsa) central to the movement, Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12 February 1922.

 

• The Non-Cooperation Movement had been launched in 1920 in response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Rowlatt Act, among other grievances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The withdrawal of the movement led to disillusionment among some younger nationalists, some of whom later turned to revolutionary/militant methods.

 

• The Civil Disobedience Movement, Gandhi's next major mass movement, was launched later in 1930 with the Dandi March.

 

NOTE

 

• Jallianwala Bagh massacre (Option 1): This 1919 tragedy was actually a trigger that led to the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement, not its withdrawal.

 

• Bengal partition (Option 3): The 1905 partition of Bengal led to the Swadeshi Movement, not the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

• Round Table conferences (Option 4): These conferences (1930-32) were held after the Civil Disobedience Movement, unrelated to the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

question: The Kashi Yatra Scheme was introduced by the government of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kashi Yatra Scheme was introduced by the Government of Karnataka in 2022, under Chief Minister Basavaraj Bommai, to enable elderly pilgrims from the state to visit the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi. (काशी यात्रा योजना — कर्नाटक सरकार)

 

• Under the scheme, the state government provides financial assistance/subsidy towards travel expenses for eligible senior pilgrims undertaking the Kashi Yatra.

 

• The scheme gained relevance following the redevelopment of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi, inaugurated in December 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Several Indian states run similar pilgrimage-assistance schemes for senior citizens, such as the Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra Yojana in states like Madhya Pradesh and Punjab.

 

• Karnataka's scheme is administered through its Muzrai (religious endowments) Department.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2), Punjab (Option 3) and Kerala (Option 4): These states are not the ones that introduced the Kashi Yatra Scheme; it is a Karnataka government initiative.

question: The national highway network connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golden Quadrilateral.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golden Quadrilateral is a network of high-speed national highways connecting India's four largest metropolitan cities — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata — forming a quadrilateral shape. (गोल्डन क्वाड्रिलेटरल — दिल्ली-मुंबई-चेन्नई-कोलकाता)

 

• It is the largest highway project in India and the fifth-longest in the world, spanning about 5,846 km, implemented under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP).

 

• The project was launched in 2001 during the tenure of Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related highway corridors include the North-South Corridor (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) and the East-West Corridor (Silchar to Porbandar).

 

• The Golden Quadrilateral is managed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

 

NOTE

 

• Diamond quadrilateral (Option 1) and Diamond polygon (Option 2): "Diamond Quadrilateral" is actually the name of a separate high-speed rail network project connecting India's major metro cities, not the highway network; "Diamond polygon" is not a recognised term.

 

• Golden polygon (Option 3): Not the correct/official name for this highway network; the correct term is Golden Quadrilateral.

question: Synecology can be defined as which of the following?
option_1: A branch of science that deals with the interrelationship of individual species with its environment.
option_2: A branch of science that deals with the interrelationship of two species.
option_3: A branch of science that deals with the interrelationship of whole biome.
option_4: A branch of ecology that deals with the structure, development and distribution of ecological communities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A branch of ecology that deals with the structure, development and distribution of ecological communities.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Synecology, also called community ecology, is the branch of ecology that studies groups of organisms (communities) as a unit, examining their structure, development, distribution and interrelationships. (सिनइकोलॉजी — पारिस्थितिक समुदाय का अध्ययन)

 

• It contrasts with autecology, which studies the relationship of an individual species (or single organism) with its environment.

 

• Synecology examines aspects such as species composition, community structure, ecological succession and interactions between different populations within an ecosystem.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ecology is broadly divided into autecology (individual/species-level) and synecology (community-level) based on the level of organisation studied.

 

• Eugene P. Odum, often called the father of modern ecology, contributed significantly to the development of community and ecosystem ecology.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: This describes autecology (study of an individual species with its environment), not synecology.

 

• Option 2: Describes the interrelationship of only two species, which does not define synecology, which deals with whole communities.

 

• Option 3: "Whole biome" is too broad and imprecise; synecology specifically studies ecological communities, not biomes as a whole.

question: 'Thaipoosam’ festival is celebrated in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thaipoosam (Thaipusam) is a Hindu festival primarily celebrated by the Tamil community, notably in Tamil Nadu, dedicated to Lord Murugan (Kartikeya). (थाईपूसम — तमिलनाडु)

 

• It falls in the Tamil month of Thai (January–February), on the day the moon passes through the star Pusam, commemorating the occasion when Goddess Parvati gave Lord Murugan a spear (Vel) to vanquish the demon Soorapadman.

 

• Devotees observe the festival with acts of devotion including carrying kavadis (ornamented structures) and, in some cases, body piercings, as a form of penance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Thaipoosam is also celebrated with great fervour by Tamil communities outside India, notably at the Batu Caves in Malaysia and in Singapore.

 

• Major Murugan temples associated with the festival in Tamil Nadu include Palani, Tiruchendur and Tiruttani.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1), Andhra Pradesh (Option 2) and Goa (Option 4): Thaipoosam is not a traditional or major festival of these states; it is distinctively associated with the Tamil community and Tamil Nadu.

question: The Kuchipudi dance form originated in which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh, from which it derives its name. (कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• It is traditionally a dance-drama performance, historically performed by male Brahmin dancers, and combines elements of Natya (drama), Nritta (pure dance) and Nritya (expressive dance).

 

• It draws its theoretical base from the ancient Natya Shastra and became especially popular through Siddhendra Yogi, credited as a key figure in its development in the 17th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's eight classical dance forms are: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• A well-known Kuchipudi item is the Tarangam, performed by the dancer balancing on the rim of a brass plate.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Associated with Kathak, not Kuchipudi.

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Associated with Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, not Kuchipudi.

 

• Assam (Option 3): Associated with Sattriya, not Kuchipudi.

question: The SI unit of speed is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is m/s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SI (International System of Units) unit of speed is metre per second (m/s), derived from the base SI units of length (metre) and time (second). (गति की SI इकाई — मीटर प्रति सेकंड)

 

• Speed is a scalar quantity defined as the distance travelled per unit time, and its SI unit follows directly from the SI base units for distance and time.

 

• Units like km/hr are commonly used in everyday contexts (e.g., vehicle speed) but are not the SI unit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Velocity, a vector quantity, also has the SI unit m/s, since it is displacement per unit time.

 

• To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18; to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

 

NOTE

 

• km/s (Option 2), km/hr (Option 3) and m/hr (Option 4): These are all valid units for expressing speed in various contexts, but none of them is the SI unit, which is specifically m/s.

question: On the occasion of teacher’s day 2022, the Indian Science Technology and Engineering facilities Map (I-STEM) launched an initiative to strengthen the efforts of scientifically inclined women. What is the name of this initiative?
solution_text:
The correct answer is WEST.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On Teacher's Day, 5 September 2022, the Indian Science, Technology and Engineering facilities Map (I-STEM) launched the "Women in Engineering, Science and Technology" (WEST) initiative. (वेस्ट पहल — विज्ञान में महिलाएं)

 

• The initiative aims to strengthen the efforts of scientifically inclined women, including those who took a career break, by connecting them with mentors, laboratories and research facilities across the country.

 

• I-STEM itself is a national web portal that maps and shares publicly funded research facilities/equipment across Indian institutions, functioning under the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The WEST initiative particularly targets women researchers who face career gaps and seeks to reintegrate them into mainstream scientific research.

 

• I-STEM was launched in 2020 to promote sharing of research infrastructure among scientists and researchers in India.

 

NOTE

 

• KUSUM (Option 1): Refers to the Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan, a solar energy scheme for farmers, unrelated to this I-STEM initiative.

 

• KALYAN (Option 2) and NAMASTE (Option 4): These are not the names of the I-STEM initiative for women scientists launched on Teacher's Day 2022; the correct name is WEST.

question: The first English Factory in Bengal set up on the banks of river “Hugli” in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1651.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first English factory in Bengal was established at Hugli (Hooghly), on the banks of the river Hugli, in 1651, following permission granted by Shah Shuja, the Mughal governor of Bengal. (हुगली — पहली अंग्रेज़ी फैक्ट्री, 1651)

 

• This factory was set up primarily to trade in items such as saltpetre, textiles and silk, and marked the beginning of formal English East India Company presence in Bengal.

 

• The English later expanded their presence in Bengal, eventually founding Calcutta (Kolkata) in 1690 under Job Charnock.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The English East India Company had earlier established its first Indian factory at Surat in 1613.

 

• Other early English factories in India included those at Madras (1639) and Bombay (acquired in 1668).

 

NOTE

 

• 1671 (Option 1), 1641 (Option 2) and 1661 (Option 3): These years are incorrect; the first English factory in Bengal, at Hugli, was established specifically in 1651.

question: In which of the following cities did Prime Minister Narendra Modi participate in 2019 as part of the celebration of International Day of Yoga on June 21?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ranchi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The main event of the 5th International Day of Yoga, on 21 June 2019, was held at the Prabhat Tara Ground in Ranchi, Jharkhand, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय योग दिवस 2019 — रांची)

 

• Around 40,000 people participated in the mass yoga demonstration alongside PM Modi at this event.

 

• The International Day of Yoga is observed every year on 21 June, following its adoption by the United Nations General Assembly in December 2014 on India's proposal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The theme for International Day of Yoga 2019 was "Yoga for Climate Action".

 

• PM Modi has led the main Yoga Day event at different locations in different years, including New Delhi's Rajpath (2015), Chandigarh (2016), Lucknow (2017) and Dehradun/FRI (2018).

 

NOTE

 

• Lucknow (Option 2), New Delhi (Option 3) and Chandigarh (Option 4): These cities hosted the main Yoga Day event led by PM Modi in other years (2017, 2015, and 2016 respectively), not in 2019, when the venue was Ranchi.

question: What should be the standard length of a tennis court according the laws of the International Tennis Federation (ITF), 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 23.77 m.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the rules of the International Tennis Federation (ITF), a standard tennis court is 23.77 metres (78 feet) long. (टेनिस कोर्ट — 23.77 मीटर लंबा)

 

• The width of the court is 8.23 metres (27 feet) for singles matches and 10.97 metres (36 feet) for doubles matches.

 

• The court is divided into two equal halves by a net, with the net height being 0.914 m (3 feet) at the centre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tennis is played on various surfaces, including grass (e.g., Wimbledon), clay (e.g., French Open) and hard courts (e.g., US Open, Australian Open).

 

• The ITF (International Tennis Federation), founded in 1913, is the world governing body for the sport of tennis.

 

NOTE

 

• 22.45 m (Option 2), 26.42 m (Option 3) and 25.34 m (Option 4): These figures are all incorrect; the standard, ITF-specified length of a tennis court is 23.77 m.

question: Article 20 of the Constitution of India deals with ______________.
option_1: protection of life and personal liberty
option_2: protection in respect of conviction for offences
solution_text:
The correct answer is protection in respect of conviction for offences.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 20 of the Indian Constitution provides "Protection in respect of conviction for offences", a fundamental right available to both citizens and non-citizens. (अनुच्छेद 20 — अपराधों के लिए दोषसिद्धि के संबंध में संरक्षण)

 

• It guarantees three protections: no ex-post-facto conviction (no punishment under a law not in force when the act was committed), protection against double jeopardy (no repeated prosecution for the same offence), and protection against self-incrimination (no person can be compelled to be a witness against themselves).

 

• Article 20, along with Article 21 (protection of life and personal liberty) and Article 22 (protection against arrest and detention), together form the "Right to Life and Personal Liberty" cluster under Part III of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike most fundamental rights, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Article 359.

 

• Article 17 deals with the abolition of untouchability, and Article 21A deals with the right to education.

 

NOTE

 

• Protection of life and personal liberty (Option 1): This is dealt with under Article 21, not Article 20.

 

• Abolition of untouchability (Option 3): This is dealt with under Article 17, not Article 20.

 

• Right to education (Option 4): This is dealt with under Article 21A, not Article 20.

question: Who is the father of the modern ecology?
solution_text:
The correct answer is E P Odum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Eugene Pleasants Odum (E. P. Odum), an American biologist, is widely regarded as the "father of modern ecology" for his pioneering work in ecosystem ecology. (ई. पी. ओडम — आधुनिक पारिस्थितिकी के जनक)

 

• His influential 1953 textbook, "Fundamentals of Ecology", co-authored with his brother Howard T. Odum, was one of the first to present ecology as a distinct, unified scientific discipline centred on the ecosystem concept.

 

• Odum's work emphasised the flow of energy and nutrients through ecosystems, laying the foundation for modern ecosystem science.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term "ecology" itself was coined by German biologist Ernst Haeckel in 1866.

 

• Arthur Tansley, a British ecologist, is credited with coining the term "ecosystem" in 1935.

 

NOTE

 

• Robert Brown (Option 1): A Scottish botanist known for discovering the cell nucleus and Brownian motion, not linked to founding modern ecology.

 

• Charles Darwin (Option 2): Known for the theory of evolution by natural selection, an important influence on biology broadly, but not specifically credited as the father of modern ecology.

 

• Robert Hook (Option 4): Known for discovering and naming the "cell" using a microscope, not for founding modern ecology.

question: Which of the following Indian states receive rainfall during October and November due to the North-East monsoon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamil Nadu receives the bulk of its annual rainfall from the North-East (retreating) monsoon, which occurs during October, November and December. (तमिलनाडु — पूर्वोत्तर मानसून वर्षा)

 

• During this season, winds blow from land to sea (north-east direction), but they pick up moisture while crossing the Bay of Bengal and bring rain to the south-eastern coast of India, particularly Tamil Nadu, southern Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Karnataka and Kerala.

 

• This is in contrast to most of the rest of India, which receives the bulk of its rainfall from the South-West monsoon (June to September).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North-East monsoon is also called the "retreating monsoon" since it follows the withdrawal of the South-West monsoon from the Indian subcontinent.

 

• Cities such as Chennai receive a substantial share of their annual rainfall during this October-December period, often associated with cyclonic activity in the Bay of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1), Maharashtra (Option 2) and Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): These states receive the bulk of their rainfall from the South-West monsoon (June-September), not primarily from the North-East monsoon.

question: Who is the Ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prime Minister of India serves as the Ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India). (नीति आयोग — प्रधानमंत्री पदेन अध्यक्ष)

 

• NITI Aayog was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission, as the premier policy think tank of the Government of India, providing strategic and technical advice.

 

• Other key functionaries of NITI Aayog include a Vice-Chairperson (appointed by the PM), a CEO, and a Governing Council comprising all State Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog was Arvind Panagariya; as of 2022, the Vice-Chairperson is Suman Bery.

 

• NITI Aayog also has full-time and part-time members, along with ex-officio members drawn from the Union Council of Ministers.

 

NOTE

 

• President (Option 1), Home Minister (Option 3) and Finance Minister (Option 4): None of these office-holders serves as the ex-officio chairman of NITI Aayog; that role is held by the Prime Minister.

question:
Which of the following statements is true?

A)Wage bill of the government is a capital expenditure.

B) Disinvestment by the government in a company is a capital receipt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only (B).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement B is correct: Disinvestment (the government selling its stake/shares in a public sector company) is classified as a capital receipt, since it reduces government assets and does not create a future liability. (विनिवेश — पूंजीगत प्राप्ति)

 

• Statement A is incorrect: The wage bill (salaries) of the government is classified as revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure, since it is a recurring expense that does not create any asset or reduce any liability.

 

• Capital expenditure refers to spending that creates assets (e.g., building infrastructure) or reduces liabilities (e.g., repaying loans), whereas revenue expenditure covers the routine, day-to-day running costs of government (e.g., salaries, subsidies, interest payments).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Capital receipts include disinvestment proceeds, market borrowings, and recovery of loans; revenue receipts include tax revenue and non-tax revenue like fees and fines.

 

• The government's overall budget is divided into the Revenue Budget (revenue receipts and expenditure) and the Capital Budget (capital receipts and expenditure).

 

NOTE

 

• Only (A) (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement A wrongly classifies the wage bill as capital expenditure, when it is actually revenue expenditure.

 

• Neither (A) nor (B) (Option 2): Incorrect, since Statement B is factually correct.

 

• Both (A) and (B) (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement A is factually wrong.

question: Who has been appointed as the 37th CRPF Director General?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sujoy Lal Thaosen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sujoy Lal Thaosen, an IPS officer of the 1988 batch (Assam-Meghalaya cadre), took charge as the 37th Director General of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in October 2022. (सुजॉय लाल थाओसेन — 37वें CRPF महानिदेशक)

 

• He succeeded Kuldiep Singh as CRPF Director General.

 

• The CRPF (Central Reserve Police Force) is India's largest Central Armed Police Force, primarily responsible for internal security, counter-insurgency and law-and-order duties, headquartered in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CRPF traces its origin to the Crown Representative's Police, established in 1939, and was renamed CRPF after India's independence in 1949.

 

• The CRPF's specialised units include the Rapid Action Force (RAF) and the COBRA (Commando Battalion for Resolute Action).

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra Kumar (Option 1), Anil Chauhan (Option 3) and Vijay Jasuja (Option 4): None of these officers was appointed as the 37th CRPF Director General; the correct officer is Sujoy Lal Thaosen. (Notably, General Anil Chauhan was separately appointed India's Chief of Defence Staff around this time, an unrelated position.)

question: Who among the following gave up his traditional professions and took to arms, successfully established kingdom in Karnataka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kadamba Mayurasharman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mayurasharman (Mayuravarman), a Brahmin scholar, founded the Kadamba dynasty in Karnataka in the 4th century CE (c. 345 CE), with its capital at Banavasi. (मयूरशर्मन — कदंब वंश, कर्नाटक)

 

• According to tradition, he was studying at Kanchipuram when he was humiliated by Pallava guards; angered by this, he gave up his traditional Brahmanical/priestly profession, took to arms, and, after defeating local chieftains and even challenging the Pallavas, established the independent Kadamba kingdom.

 

• The Kadambas were one of the earliest native ruling dynasties of Karnataka, marking a significant point in the region's political history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kadambas of Banavasi were later succeeded/absorbed by larger dynasties such as the Chalukyas of Badami.

 

• The Kadamba emblem (Kadamba tree) and script are notable elements of Karnataka's historical and cultural heritage.

 

NOTE

 

• Vasudeva Kanva (Option 1): Founder of the Kanva dynasty, which succeeded the Shungas in the Gangetic plains, not related to establishing a kingdom in Karnataka via taking up arms after abandoning a traditional profession.

 

• Gurjara-Pratihara Harichandra (Option 2): Founded the Pratihara dynasty and ruled around Jodhpur/Marwar, Rajasthan, not Karnataka.

 

• Pushyamitra Shunga (Option 3): Founder of the Shunga dynasty, a senapati (military commander) under the Mauryas who overthrew the last Maurya ruler; he ruled in the region of Magadha/central India, not Karnataka.
